name: PMSM · Field-oriented control
description: A 1500 rpm speed command with cascaded d/q current control. The speed PI asks for q-axis current (torque); the d-axis reference is zero. Two current PIs set the d/q voltages, which turn back into three phase voltages through the inverse Park (the Park transform fed −θe) and inverse Clarke transforms and drive a controlled three-phase source, the ideal model of an inverter. The machine is the Modelica permanent-magnet synchronous machine with its inductances and magnet voltage set explicitly; its load is a damper plus a torque step that raises the load from 0.05 N·m to 0.4 N·m at 0.45 s. Measured phase currents come back through the Clarke and Park transforms; the rotor angle comes from an angle sensor scaled by the pole pairs.
